evidence.thesis: DeepSeek-V3 is a 671B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model with 37B activated parameters that, through MLA, DeepSeekMoE, an auxiliary-loss-free load-balancing strategy, multi-token prediction, FP8 mixed-precision training, and infrastructure co-design, achieves performance comparable to leading closed-source models while requiring only 2.788M H800 GPU hours for full training.
evidence.plain_summary: The paper introduces DeepSeek-V3, a large open-source Mixture-of-Experts language model with 671B total parameters, of which 37B are active per token. It combines efficient attention and expert architectures with two new techniques: load balancing without an auxiliary loss and training to predict multiple future tokens. The authors also describe an FP8 mixed-precision training framework and system optimizations that sharply reduce training cost while keeping training stable. After pre-training on 14.8T tokens and post-training with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, DeepSeek-V3 outperforms other open-source models and approaches GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet on many benchmarks. The full training reportedly costs only $5.576M at assumed H800 rental rates.
evidence.research_question: Can a very large open-source Mixture-of-Experts language model be trained efficiently and stably at scale while matching or approaching the performance of leading closed-source models?

claims.statement: Pre-training DeepSeek-V3 on each trillion tokens requires only 180K H800 GPU hours, equivalent to 3.7 days on a 2048-H800-GPU cluster.
DeepSeek-V3 trails GPT-4o and Claude-Sonnet-3.5 in English factual knowledge (SimpleQA) but surpasses them in Chinese factual knowledge (Chinese SimpleQA).
DeepSeek-V2 validated that MLA and DeepSeekMoE can maintain robust model performance while achieving efficient training and inference.
DeepSeek-V3 achieves 88.5 on MMLU, 75.9 on MMLU-Pro, and 59.1 on GPQA, outperforming all other open-source models on educational benchmarks.
DeepSeek-V3 is the top-performing model on coding competition benchmarks such as LiveCodeBench and outperforms all other models on engineering tasks except Claude-Sonnet-3.5.
DeepSeek-V3 is a Mixture-of-Experts language model with 671B total parameters, of which 37B are activated per token.
DeepSeek-V3 adopts Group Relative Policy Optimization, which foregoes a critic model and estimates the baseline from group scores.
DeepSeek-V3 achieves a win rate of over 86% against GPT-4-0314 on Arena-Hard and is the first open-source model to surpass 85% on that benchmark.
DeepSeek-V3 outperforms both closed-source and open-source models on AlpacaEval 2.0 and surpasses DeepSeek-V2.5-0905 by 20%.
A sample masking strategy is used during SFT so packed examples remain isolated and mutually invisible.
Constitutional AI with voting evaluation results from DeepSeek-V3 itself is used as a feedback source for broader contexts during development.
The total training cost of DeepSeek-V3 is $5.576M assuming an H800 rental price of $2 per GPU hour.
DeepSeek-V3-Base is claimed to be the strongest open-source base model currently available, especially in code and math.
Full training of DeepSeek-V3 requires only 2.788M H800 GPU hours.
Non-reasoning data was generated using DeepSeek-V2.5 and verified by human annotators.
Block-wise quantization of activation gradients leads to model divergence on an approximately 16B-parameter MoE model trained for around 300B tokens.
DeepSeek-V3 surpasses Qwen2.5-72B by 16.4 points on Chinese SimpleQA.
DeepSeek-V3 stands as the best-performing open-source chat model and is competitive against frontier closed-source models like GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
DeepSeek-V3 performs well across all context window lengths up to 128K on the Needle In A Haystack test.
The multi-token prediction depth D is set to 1, meaning each token predicts one additional token beyond the next token.
Reasoning post-training data is generated using an internal DeepSeek-R1 model.
DeepSeek-V3 is pre-trained on 14.8 trillion diverse and high-quality tokens.
The auxiliary-loss-free model demonstrates greater expert specialization patterns than the auxiliary-loss-based model.
Batch-wise load balancing methods face potential efficiency challenges including load imbalance within sequences or small batches and domain-shift-induced load imbalance during inference.
DeepSeek-V3-Base is fine-tuned for two epochs using cosine decay learning rate scheduling starting at 5e-6 and decreasing to 1e-6.
The context extension uses YaRN applied exclusively to the decoupled shared key k_R_t.
Each MoE layer in DeepSeek-V3 consists of 1 shared expert and 256 routed experts, with 8 routed experts activated per token.
On DROP, DeepSeek-V3 achieves an F1 score of 91.6 in the 3-shot setting, outperforming all other models in this category.
Training DeepSeek-V3 on each trillion tokens requires only 180K H800 GPU hours, which is cheaper than training 72B or 405B dense models.
DeepSeek-V3 achieves state-of-the-art performance on math-related benchmarks among non-long-CoT open-source and closed-source models, even outperforming o1-preview on MATH-500.
The auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy minimizes performance degradation from encouraging load balancing.
The DualPipe algorithm is designed for efficient pipeline parallelism with fewer pipeline bubbles and hides most communication during training.
In 1B MoE experiments, validation losses were 2.258 for sequence-wise auxiliary loss, 2.253 for auxiliary-loss-free, and 2.253 for batch-wise auxiliary loss.
DeepSeek-V3 pioneers an auxiliary-loss-free strategy for load balancing.
DeepSeek-V3 achieves average RewardBench performance on par with the best versions of GPT-4o-0806 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet-1022 while surpassing other versions.
DeepSeek-V3 outperforms all baselines on HumanEval-Mul and LiveCodeBench in algorithmic tasks.
The MTP loss weight lambda is set to 0.3 for the first 10T tokens and 0.1 for the remaining 4.8T tokens.
Rule-based reward models are used for questions verifiable by specific rules, such as math problems and LeetCode problems.
The pre-training maximum sequence length is set to 4K.
DeepSeek-V3 outperforms other open-source models and achieves performance comparable to leading closed-source models.
DeepSeek-V3 falls behind GPT-4o and Claude-Sonnet on SimpleQA primarily due to its design focus and resource allocation, with more training tokens assigned to learn Chinese knowledge.
DeepSeek-V3 extends context length first to 32K and then to 128K in two stages.
The acceptance rate of the second token prediction ranges between 85% and 90% across various generation topics.
The paper validates FP8 mixed precision training on an extremely large-scale model for the first time.
RL incorporates prompts from diverse domains including coding, math, writing, role-playing, and question answering.
R1-generated data has issues such as overthinking, poor formatting, and excessive length.
Reasoning capability from DeepSeek-R1 series models is distilled into DeepSeek-V3 during post-training.
On AIME, MATH-500, and CNMO 2024, DeepSeek-V3 outperforms the second-best model Qwen2.5 72B by approximately 10% in absolute scores.
The SFT dataset for DeepSeek-V3 includes 1.5M instances spanning multiple domains.
Model-based reward models are trained from DeepSeek-V3 SFT checkpoints and use preference data that includes chain-of-thought leading to the reward.
The auxiliary-loss-free model tends to have greater expert specialization across all layers than the auxiliary-loss-based baseline.
Although DeepSeek-V3 achieved end-to-end generation speed more than two times that of DeepSeek-V2, there remains potential for further enhancement.
The auxiliary-loss-free balancing strategy consistently achieves better model performance than purely auxiliary-loss-based methods on most evaluation benchmarks.
DeepSeek-V3 adopts Multi-head Latent Attention and DeepSeekMoE architectures.
The Multi-Token Prediction objective is found beneficial to model performance and can also be used for speculative decoding.
MTP with speculative decoding delivers 1.8 times tokens per second.
DeepSeek-V3 comprises 671B total parameters with 37B activated per token under its model hyper-parameter configuration.
DeepSeek-V3 has a limitation that its recommended deployment unit is relatively large, which might burden small-sized teams.
Distillation from DeepSeek-R1 improves LiveCodeBench and MATH-500 performance but substantially increases average response length.
The training process of DeepSeek-V3 was remarkably stable, with no irrecoverable loss spikes or rollbacks.
The MTP strategy consistently enhances model performance on most evaluation benchmarks in ablations at small and large scales.
DeepSeek-V3 replaces all FFNs except for the first three layers with MoE layers.
FP8 training with high-precision accumulation and fine-grained quantization keeps relative error below 0.25% compared with BF16 training.
DeepSeek-V3-Base achieves the best performance on most benchmarks, especially on math and code tasks, among the compared base models.
The stated training costs exclude prior research and ablation experiments on architectures, algorithms, or data.

generated_sections.title: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models
generated_sections.content: General background: A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model is a neural network architecture in which some components (typically feed-forward sublayers) are replaced by a set of expert modules plus a routing mechanism, so that only a subset of experts is activated for each token. This keeps total parameter count large while reducing computation per token. This paper's setting is DeepSeek-V3, which is described as a Mixture-of-Experts language model with 671B total parameters, of which 37B are activated per token. Its architecture replaces all feed-forward networks (FFNs) except for the first three layers with MoE layers. Each MoE layer consists of 1 shared expert and 256 routed experts, with each expert's intermediate hidden dimension being 2048; among the routed experts, 8 are activated per token, and each token is ensured to be sent to at most 4 nodes.

generated_sections.title: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and architecture validation
generated_sections.content: General background: Attention mechanisms are the components that let a language model weigh different token positions when forming representations; multi-head attention uses multiple parallel attention heads. The paper adopts Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), a specific attention architecture, together with DeepSeekMoE, stating that these architectures were thoroughly validated in DeepSeek-V2. The preceding DeepSeek-V2 work is cited as having demonstrated that MLA and DeepSeekMoE can maintain robust model performance while achieving efficient training and inference.

generated_sections.title: Token pre-training data and sequence length
generated_sections.content: General background: Pre-training is the initial large-scale training phase in which a language model learns from raw token sequences before instruction tuning. This paper pre-trains DeepSeek-V3 on 14.8 trillion diverse and high-quality tokens, with a maximum sequence length set to 4K during pre-training. After pre-training, the context length is extended in two stages, first to 32K and then to 128K.

generated_sections.title: Context extension with YaRN
generated_sections.content: General background: Context extension techniques modify or rescale positional information so that a model trained on shorter sequences can handle longer contexts. This paper uses YaRN for context extension, configured consistently with DeepSeek-V2, and applies it exclusively to the decoupled shared key k_R_t. This sits within the two-stage extension described in the paper, from 4K pre-training length to 32K and then to 128K.

generated_sections.title: FP8 mixed precision training at scale
generated_sections.content: General background: Mixed precision training uses lower-precision numeric formats for some computations to reduce memory and compute cost, while usually retaining higher precision where needed for stability. This paper introduces an FP8 mixed precision training framework and states that it validates its effectiveness on an extremely large-scale model for the first time.

generated_sections.title: Pipeline parallelism and DualPipe
generated_sections.content: General background: Pipeline parallelism splits a model's layers across devices and processes micro-batches in a pipeline, but it can suffer from pipeline bubbles, i.e., idle periods while stages wait for work. This paper designs the DualPipe algorithm for efficient pipeline parallelism, reporting that it has fewer pipeline bubbles and hides most communication during training through computation-communication overlap.

generated_sections.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
generated_sections.content: General background: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is a post-pre-training stage in which a model is trained on curated instruction-response examples to follow instructions and perform tasks. It fine-tunes DeepSeek-V3-Base for two epochs on this SFT dataset using cosine decay learning rate scheduling that starts at 5e-6 and gradually decreases to 1e-6. During post-training, it distills reasoning capability from the DeepSeek-R1 series of models into DeepSeek-V3 while carefully maintaining balance between model accuracy and other considerations.

stories.title: DeepSeek-V3: The $5.576M Model That Challenged the Giants
stories.dek: A 671B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model, trained for a reported $5.576M and 2.788M H800 GPU hours, matches or approaches leading closed-source models while introducing auxiliary-loss-free load balancing and FP8 training at scale.

closing.body: DeepSeek-V3 shows that an open-source Mixture-of-Experts model can be trained efficiently and stably at scale, reaching performance comparable to leading closed-source models on many benchmarks. Its efficiency comes from architecture, FP8 mixed precision, and infrastructure co-design, not just raw compute. But the paper is candid about limits: the recommended deployment unit is relatively large and may burden small teams; generation speed, though more than twice DeepSeek-V2, still has room for improvement; and the headline training cost excludes prior research and ablation experiments. The core question — how far this recipe scales — is left open.

source_references.excerpt: We present DeepSeek-V3, a strong Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 671B total parameters with 37B activated for each token.
To achieve efficient inference and cost-effective training, DeepSeek-V3 adopts Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE architec-tures, which were thoroughly validated in DeepSeek-V2.
Furthermore, DeepSeek-V3 pioneers an auxiliary-loss-free strategy for load balancing and sets a multi-token prediction training objective for stronger performance.
